bullets: Wreck penetration is a planning problem first, a buoyancy problem second — internalizing that ordering makes the downstream decisions easier.

Silt-out from poor finning technique kills more divers in wrecks than equipment failures, so technique deserves more attention than gear; the second-order effects of that risk are what most people miss.
Erosion on a wreck site changes the dive every season, meaning a site known one year cannot be assumed identical the next.
DAN's safety stops aren't suggestions — this is where dive planning and wreck diving intersect.
Framing determines which trade-offs a diver is actually making; decisions evaluated explicitly rather than by default avoid rebuilding the approach from scratch a year later.
Soil erosion cross-cuts every other wreck-diving consideration, affecting planning, site conditions, and risk together rather than acting as an isolated factor.
Running one idea for two weeks is the recommended starting point, with iteration rather than wholesale change driving improvement.
